items.title: Guard jq-to-mv writes in core orchestrator against jq failure
items.intent: Backlog files must never be corrupted by a failed jq command — every jq-to-mv write must verify jq succeeded before overwriting the original file.
items.description: In .aishore/aishore, the pattern jq ... > $tmp followed by mv $tmp $file does not check jq exit code. If jq fails, mv overwrites the original with empty/corrupt data. Affected functions: update_item(), remove_item(), create_sprint(). Guard each with: jq ... > $tmp || { rm -f $tmp; log_error ...; return 1; }
steps: Find all 'jq ... > $tmp' patterns in .aishore/aishore (roughly 5-8 instances)
For each instance, add jq exit code check before the mv command
Ensure rm -f $tmp runs on jq failure to avoid stale temp files

acceptanceCriteria.text: No jq output redirect to tmp file is followed by mv without checking jq exit code

items.title: Unquoted variable in JSON construction breaks AC entries
items.intent: Acceptance criteria containing quotes or special characters must round-trip safely — JSON construction must use jq, never string interpolation with unquoted variables.
items.description: In cmd-backlog-write.sh, $last_text is embedded unquoted in a JSON object literal when attaching --ac-verify to the preceding --ac. If the AC text contains double quotes, braces, or backslashes, the JSON breaks. Replace with jq -n --arg for safe construction.
steps: In cmd-backlog-write.sh, find the two locations where ac_entries constructs JSON with string interpolation
Replace each with: jq -n --argjson text "$last_text" --arg verify "$2" '{text: $text, verify: $verify}'

acceptanceCriteria.text: No raw string interpolation of last_text in JSON construction

items.title: Module load failures silently marked as loaded
items.intent: A broken module must fail fast at load time — silently marking a failed source as loaded causes cryptic command-not-found errors far from the root cause.
items.description: _load_module() runs source $mod_file then sets _LOADED_MODULES[$mod]=1 regardless of whether source succeeded. Add error check after source.
steps: In _load_module(), wrap source with: source "$mod_file" || { log_error "Failed to load module $mod"; return 1; }
Only set _LOADED_MODULES[$mod]=1 after source succeeds

acceptanceCriteria.text: _load_module checks source exit code before marking module as loaded

items.title: sed injection in cmd-init.sh via unescaped user input
items.intent: User-provided project names and commands must never be interpreted as sed metacharacters — init wizard input must be escaped before sed substitution.
items.description: cmd-init.sh passes $project_name and $validate_cmd directly to sed without escaping. Characters like |, &, and backslash break config files.
steps: Create a sed-escape helper or inline escape: sed 's:[&/\\]:\\&:g'
Apply escaping to variables before passing to sed

acceptanceCriteria.text: sed substitution uses escaped values, not raw user input

items.title: Missing git error handling in sprint commit flow
items.intent: Git failures during sprint commit must be detected — an undetected failure means the sprint proceeds with uncommitted work, leading to lost changes on branch cleanup.
items.description: In the sprint commit flow, git add -A and git commit run without checking exit codes. If either fails, the orchestrator continues assuming state was saved.
steps: Find git add and git commit calls in the sprint flow
Add exit code checks to each

acceptanceCriteria.text: git add calls check exit codes

items.title: Excessive || true in cmd-groom.sh masks real jq failures
items.intent: Grooming must fail visibly when jq parsing breaks — silently continuing with empty data produces corrupt or incomplete backlog edits.
items.description: cmd-groom.sh uses || true after many jq calls. When jq fails, downstream code operates on empty strings. Replace with proper error handling.
steps: Audit all jq ... || true patterns in cmd-groom.sh
Replace with proper error handling, keeping || true only where empty is a valid result

acceptanceCriteria.text: No bare || true after jq without justification comment

items.title: Worktree creation TOCTOU race between rmdir and git worktree add
items.intent: Worktree creation must be atomic — a race between mktemp/rmdir/git can cause sprint failures.
items.description: mktemp -d then rmdir then git worktree add has a race. Use mktemp -u or skip the rmdir.
steps: Remove rmdir step between mktemp and git worktree add

acceptanceCriteria.text: No rmdir between mktemp and git worktree add

items.title: Sprint merge fails when backlog files have uncommitted local changes
items.intent: Sprints must not fail at merge time due to locally modified tracking files — the orchestrator must handle its own bookkeeping files around merges.
items.description: When the orchestrator updates backlog/bugs.json or backlog/backlog.json during a sprint session (marking items done, updating failCount), those changes are uncommitted. When the next sprint's worktree branch merges back, git merge fails with 'local changes would be overwritten'. The orchestrator should stash or commit tracking changes before merge.
steps: Before merging a feature branch, stash any uncommitted changes to backlog files
After merge, pop the stash to restore tracking state
Handle stash pop conflicts gracefully

acceptanceCriteria.text: Sprint merge does not fail due to uncommitted backlog file changes

items.title: Spec refinement fails with 'sprint item spec is empty' after sprint failure
items.intent: Spec refinement must work when items fail — it exists specifically for failed items, so it must have access to the item spec at refinement time.
items.description: After sprint failure, the orchestrator attempts spec refinement but reports 'Cannot refine: sprint item spec is empty'. The sprint.json appears to be reset before refinement runs, losing the item data needed for refinement.
steps: Ensure sprint.json still contains the item spec when spec refinement is invoked
Move sprint.json reset to after refinement completes, not before

acceptanceCriteria.text: Spec refinement has access to sprint item data

items.title: Validator max turns (10) too low — causes false sprint failures
items.intent: Validators must have enough turns to complete verification — a validator hitting max turns is a system failure, not a code quality failure.
items.description: With MAX_TURNS_VALIDATOR=10, validators frequently hit the limit before writing result.json, causing the sprint to fail even when the developer's code passed all AC verify commands. Increase default to 15 or 20.
steps: Increase MAX_TURNS_VALIDATOR default from 10 to 15
Update CONFIGURATION.md if it documents the default
